LifeMode · UX · 11. november 2026

Åtte måter å leve fem år på

Åtte designkonsepter for LifeMode, tegnet i parallell fra samme PRD og samme brief. Hvert konsept viser landingsside, spillhuben, hendelser og månedsplan, en hendelse, telefonen og pengevisningen, pluss et oversiktsark over alle de andre sidene. Trykk på en skjerm for å se den større.

Konsept 1 av 8

Månedsfeed

Livet ditt fra 15 til 20 – én story om gangen.

The idea. LifeMode uses the grammar a 15-year-old already reads without thinking: stories, reactions, reposts, DMs, creator stats. Each in-game year is a story reel. The top of every screen has 12 ticks, one per month, and the four highlight months are fat ticks. Every month is one story you tap through. The point is not to parody a feed. It is to make "what did my choice do?" feel as instant as a reaction on a post.

Game dynamics

  • Monthly loop = a story. The hub (02) is the month's cover story: your room full-bleed, a caption ("Ingen hendelse. Lønna kom inn."), sticker chips for money in and out, and four highlight bubbles (Telefon, Månedsplan, Jobb, Penger). A ring on a bubble means something new. Fortsett is one lime bar, so a quiet month takes one tap.
  • Highlight event = a full-bleed story card (04a) from a sender (Mamma). The options are action cards with kroner and wellbeing on each one. One option is always free, and one you can't afford shows the missing amount.
  • Consequences = a reaction burst (04b): stickers for −1 490 kr and Stress −2 pop in and settle. Then comes the echo, a repost of your own earlier choice: "Du for 8 måneder siden: Nei takk til mobilforsikring." The same pink repost mark is used everywhere for echo badges, even in the timeline ("kan gi ekko").
  • Hvorfor? = a light bottom sheet that cuts through the dark feed. It shows a stacked cause bar (500 kr deductible + 990 kr echo) and plain text with the figures.
  • Room = the story background. New layers appear in it. Empty layers show as dashed outlines ("mopedhjelm?"), so the room also teases what you might own next.
  • Month plan shows school and work as locked, hatched blocks and free time as tappable slots. An echo chip explains why there are 3 slots instead of 4.

Visual language

Near-black Natt base, Volt lime for action, money in and "now", and Puls pink for echoes and reactions. Amber is only for missing amounts and warnings. Archivo Black carries big, confident numbers and headlines. Schibsted Grotesk, a Norwegian-made grotesk, is the precise UI voice. Shapes are pills and 20–28 px cards. Every delta has a sign and a word. Motion intent: snappy and haptic. Ticks fill as the month plays. A card advances with a short horizontal push and a tap-thud. Reaction stickers scale from 0.6 to 1.05 to 1 in 220 ms. The echo repost slides up from below, the way a reshared post appears. Nothing depends on gestures: every swipe has a tap equivalent.

Why it works for 15–20

It needs no tutorial. Ticks, rings and reposts are already understood, and the game borrows feed rhythm instead of school rhythm.

Risks

Feed grammar can read as "another app wanting my attention", so the copy must stay calm and non-addictive. Dark, saturated colour needs strict contrast discipline. The fat and thin ticks are subtle at small sizes, so they need labels.

Prototype first

The 04a → 04b moment: event, choice, reaction burst, echo repost, Hvorfor?. Then test whether players link the repost to their earlier choice.

Konsept 2 av 8

Brettspill

Fem år. 60 ruter. Hvert trekk teller.

Idea. LifeMode is a modern euro-style board game lying on a felt table. The five years are a printed saffron board: 60 squares in five serpentine rows, one row per age, with a checkered "20" finish medallion hanging off the edge. Markus is a chunky coral pawn. Money is brass coins and banknotes, choices are cards, and wellbeing is a set of score tracks with wooden markers.

Game dynamics

  • Monthly loop = one move. The hub's main button doesn't say "Continue". It says "Flytt til april", and the pawn steps one square along the year strip. Quiet squares are plain cardstock, so a quiet month really is one tap. Coral squares carry a card icon and mean you draw a highlight card. Blue key squares are age unlocks (mopedlappen at 13, card and licence at 37). A hazard-striped tile shows that a crisis can turn a quiet square active.
  • Month plan = player mat. School and work are hatched blocks printed on the mat and locked. You tap activity tiles into numbered slot spaces. Extra shifts physically cover slot 4 with a work block ("Tilbake i juni"). If you can't afford a tile, it greys out and shows "Mangler 160 kr".
  • Events = drawn cards. Options read as moves A/B/C, each with a coin cost, a word ("fra brukskonto"), and token deltas. The free option is labelled "Gratis".
  • Consequences = pieces moving. Coins slide off your stack and the stress cube steps along its track. The echo badge is a round blue token stamped "M14", linked by a dotted line back to the February square. "Hvorfor?" opens as a rulebook page with a ledger of causes. "Utsatt: mopedlappen" shows what the choice closed. The room is a player board where belongings are layers, and missing ones are printed outlines, like the dashed "mopedplass" waiting for a moped.
  • Wellbeing uses three shapes as well as three colours (cube = stress, disc = fritid, hexagon = sosialt), always with numbers and the "Ekte seier: 50+" flag.

Visual language

Teal felt ground with grain, saffron cardboard with a speckle pattern, cardstock cards, and drop-shadowed depth with a visible tile thickness. Type is Bricolage Grotesque for display (box-lid character) and Barlow Semi Condensed for tabular UI. Motion intent: one authored moment, the pawn hop plus coins sliding when you move.

Why it works for 15–20

A board game is social, physical and readable at a glance. Progress is literally visible (row 2 of 5), and the metaphor makes "every choice carries forward" spatial instead of preachy.

Risks

The screens are dense, and texture and depth may cost performance on cheap phones. The pawn on small squares can hide labels. Saffron-on-saffron panels need careful contrast for secondary text. The look could read as "family game" if the illustrations drift toward cute.

Prototype first

The hub → "Flytt til april" pawn hop → event card flip → result with the echo token flying back to its source square. Test it on the bus with a sceptical 15-year-old.

Konsept 3 av 8

Pixel-RPG

Livet ditt som 16-bit rollespill: hvert valg gir poeng, og spillet viser alltid hvorfor.

Idea. LifeMode is a 16-bit life RPG. Markus is a pixel sprite standing in a pixel room. Menus are classic bone-bordered RPG windows with a blinking cursor, and every money or wellbeing change pops up like a damage or heal number. It is a game first. The finance lives inside rules teenagers already know by heart: stats, inventory, quests and level-ups.

Game dynamics

  • Monthly loop = a turn. The hub is an overworld screen. At the top sits a 12-block year track, with gold notches on the active months. Below it is the room, the TRIVSEL stat panel (64/100, a marker at 50, and Stress/Fritid/Sosialt as segmented bars with numbers and ± deltas), four command tiles (Telefon, Månedsplan, Jobb, Penger) and a big gold FORTSETT button. A quiet month is one tap. An "!" speech bubble over the avatar's head says "2 NYE".
  • Year = world map / quest log. Months are nodes on a winding path. Highlight months are gold star tiles, an echo month carries the callback glyph, a storm cloud warns "krise?", and "NIVÅ 16 – mopedlappen låst opp" is a level-up gate. The quest log lists what is coming: an April event, a dated summer-job offer, an echo due in August, and the open moped licence with 4 150 kr missing.
  • Month plan = party/skill slots. School and work are locked equipment. There are 3 activity slots because extra shifts lock slot 4 ("tilbake i juni"). Activities are a skill list with cost and effects, placed by tapping. A missing amount shows as a locked row ("Mangler 250 kr"). There is also "Samme som forrige måned".
  • Event = dialogue with portrait + menu. Emma's pixel portrait asks the question. Each option is an action with kroner, sosialt and stress, and one is marked GRATIS.
  • Consequence = floating numbers. "−450 kr hyttetur", "+120 kr fra Emma", "+4 sosialt". The EKKO badge is a callback card that links back to the month-10 quest. Hvorfor? splits the net amount by cause. ÅPNET/LUKKET lines and the target progress (72 % → 70 %) follow. Room layers act as loot: the new piggy bank gets a "NY!" tag.

Visual language

Night-ink ground and deep menu-blue windows with notched bone borders. Gold is kroner, green is a gain, coral is a loss. Every value also carries a sign and a word. Art is crisp SVG rect grids with crispEdges, all original: Markus, Emma, Norwegian town, påskehytte. Silkscreen sets headings and labels. DotGothic16 sets body text, because it keeps long Norwegian sentences and digits readable. For motion, numbers float up and fade, the cursor blinks, and a level-up banner flashes once.

Why it works

Teens already read HP bars, loot and quest logs fluently. Money becomes stats they manage, not schoolwork. The "why" sits in the place a game always puts it: the combat log.

Risks

Retro can read as nostalgia for older players. The look is dense on small screens. Pixel faces are weak at small text sizes, which is why DotGothic16 carries the body text. Floating numbers must not replace the Hvorfor? panel.

Prototype first

The hub → FORTSETT → event → floating-number result → Hvorfor? loop, timed on a phone on a bus.

Konsept 4 av 8

Mobilen (Ly)

Fem år av livet ditt – på én oppdiktet mobil.

The idea. The whole game is the character's own phone. It runs a made-up OS called Ly (Norwegian for shelter). Its emblem is a selburose built from eight petals. The landing screen is the phone being set up: the rose is only half built, and notifications from the life ahead ("Emma: Konsert?", "Minner: For 1 år siden…", "Hege ringer …") drift over it. Then Du er 15. Ny mobil. Fem år foran deg. and Opprett bruker / Logg inn.

Game dynamics.

  • The month is the home screen. The big clock reads Mars instead of a time. A thin livslinja across the top of every screen fills as the 60 months pass. Widgets show Trivsel (number plus three bars), Penger and Rommet. Fortsett til april sits where swipe-to-unlock would be, but one tap is enough.
  • Highlight events arrive as incoming calls from the sender (Hege, the class teacher). Each answer is a big button with a money chip and wellbeing chips. Right above them is the line that creates the tension: "Mopedlappen 100 % spart".
  • Consequences appear when the call ends: delta cards, Åpnet / Lukket ("Mopedlappen i april – mangler nå 3 192 kr") and the "hvis du hadde stått over" line.
  • Echo badges are Minner notifications, the familiar "for one year ago" photo-memory pattern pointed at your own choices.
  • Hvorfor? is a dark system sheet ("Ly forklarer") that splits a change into causes and rules.
  • Room: the Rull app is the camera roll of the room, layer by layer. A dashed ghost moped shows a belonging you have not unlocked yet.
  • Year: Kalender shows the year as a timeline. Highlight months are marked with a rose, unlocks with a key and boomerang follow-ups with the Minner loop. Months that could become a crisis are noted too.
  • Activities: a friend's invitation goes into the month plan with "Legg i månedsplan".
  • Wallpaper changes with life stage.

Visual language. Night blue and warm snow-white, with Norwegian accents: multe (cloudberry orange) for actions, rogn, fjord, brunost and bjørk for the apps, and gold for Minner. The signature shape is the lapp: every icon tile, widget and option has one folded top-right corner. Icons are drawn in a 2.2-stroke line. The savings goal fills as knitted masker (stitches). Type is Bricolage Grotesque for display and Schibsted Grotesk (Norwegian-made) for UI. Plus and minus always carry a sign and a word ("−3 500 kr ut", "Sosialt +8"). Motion intent: one moment only, where the rose finishes building as setup completes.

Why it works for 15–20-year-olds. The phone is their native interface, so there is nothing new to learn. A call, a notification or a memory feels like life, not schoolwork. The setting also makes the inbox, bank and calendar logical rather than menus.

Risks. The OS chrome could crowd the content on small screens. A phone inside the real phone might feel meta or claustrophobic. The look has to stay clearly fictional so it never reads as a real banking app. Dense money screens need care.

Prototype first. The incoming-call event, then the result, then Hvorfor? as a clickable flow, together with one-tap Fortsett through a quiet month. That tests whether the call metaphor beats reading.

Konsept 5 av 8

Riso-zine

Et liv i 60 utgaver – hver måned er et nytt oppslag i din egen zine.

Idea. LifeMode is a risograph zine a Norwegian 17-year-old prints about their own life: one issue per month, 60 in all. It uses off-white paper, fluor pink and riso blue printed off-register over black, halftones, torn scraps, tape, stamps and margin scribbles. The page number is the month ("s. 15").

Game dynamics

  • The loop is a page turn. Each month opens as a new spread with the month name huge, a sticker reading "måned 15 av 60", the room collage, a balance receipt and a wellbeing stamp. A quiet month gets a scribble ("ett trykk, så er du i april") and one torn ticket: Fortsett til april.
  • Choices are stickers you tap down. Options state "Koster 1 290 kr · stress −1". The free option is taped "GRATIS VALG". An activity you can't afford is striped and locked: "mangler 342 kr".
  • Consequences are receipts. A result prints before → after values with a BETALT stamp. The margin talks back: "← sparte 441 kr på forsikring. betalte 1 290 nå. hmm."
  • Echo badges are taped-in scraps of an earlier page ("s. 8: nei til forsikring"), so carrying a choice forward becomes something you can see.
  • Hvorfor? is a fold-out note with numbered causes. Åpnet and Lukket seg litt sit underneath it.
  • The room is cut-paper layers (4 of 6), each with a typed caption.

Visual language

Three inks overprinting with multiply. Big Shoulders Display is the ransom-note headline face. Courier Prime is the typewriter face for all body text and numbers, and its monospace keeps figures aligned. Permanent Marker is for scribbles only. Motion: stickers slap down with a small overshoot, and a new month arrives as a page turn.

Why it works for 15–20

It draws on DIY, collage and sticker culture, not school or bank visuals. Money shown as receipts is money teens already read.

Risks

Texture can turn into noise, so body text sits on plain paper and only display type misregisters. Fluor pink is never used as text; pink text is #B3125F. Rotation on interactive elements stays at 1–2° or less. Filters and blend modes need a performance check on cheap phones.

Prototype first

The 03b sticker month plan (tap slot, tap sticker) and the 04b result receipt with the taped echo and the Hvorfor? fold-out.

Konsept 6 av 8

Rommet

Rommet ditt er spillet: trykk på telefonen, kalenderen, sparegrisen eller forkleet – og se rommet vokse med valgene dine.

The idea. The player's bedroom is the whole interface. An isometric diorama fills the hub, and each system lives in an object: the phone on the bed opens messages, the wall calendar opens the year and the month plan, the piggy bank opens the money "kassabok", and the work apron opens the job view. The window shows the month and the street, where the moped is parked once you own one. Belongings collect over five years, so the room becomes a portrait of the life you lived.

Game dynamics. A month opens with the room reacting: the phone glows with new messages, and the calendar flips. A quiet month is one "Fortsett til april" tap. An active month is a scene: the room dims to a spotlight on the object involved (a cracked phone), and the sender speaks in a bubble. The options are actions with signed kroner and wellbeing effects, and one is always free. The result returns to the room: the phone is whole again, the deltas show as worded chips, an echo badge ("Ekko fra måned 1: pengegaven") links this month's interest to an old choice, "Hvorfor?" expands in place, and "Lukket/Åpent" shows what moved. The month plan is sticky notes on the calendar page: school and work are locked, hatched blocks, and you tap an activity into a free slot. Activities you can't afford show "Mangler 1 010 kr". Stress makes the room messier and dimmer, but wellbeing and its three parts are always written as numbers too.

Visual language. A warm Scandinavian interior: oat walls, pine-green panelling, a birch floor, a rust rug and ochre lamplight. The landing is a night scene with the room glowing. Type is Fraunces (warm display) plus Atkinson Hyperlegible (legible numbers on a bus). The isometric projection is real, with wall items skewed onto the walls.

Why it works for 15–20. It's their own space, not a bank. Filling the room is a cozy-game reward loop.

Risks. Discoverability depends on the labels, so every object has a permanent text tag and a menu route stays. Illustration cost grows with 6 layers × states. The room must stay readable at 320 px.

Prototype first. The labelled hub room and the event scene → result flow, to test whether players find the phone and calendar unaided.

Konsept 7 av 8

Kortstokk

Spill kortene. Lev med dem.

Idea. LifeMode as a roguelike deckbuilder: each month is a turn, free time is your energy (1–4 slots), school and work are locked cards on the board, and everything entering your life arrives as a card. A run is 60 turns, 15 to 20.

Game dynamics

  • Turn: the hub ("brettet") shows a 60-segment run meter, balance, trivsel 58/100 with three numbered parts, the room as player card, and four decks (Telefon, Månedsplan, Jobb, Penger). "Avslutt mars" ends the turn; a quiet month is one tap.
  • The phone deals your hand: Emma's invitation becomes a "Konsert med Emma" card valid this month only. Tap card, tap slot; no drag.
  • Slots are mana: extra shifts lock the fourth token. Cards show kr cost and STRESS/SOSIALT stats with sign and word; unaffordable cards are hatched with "MANGLER 430 kr".
  • Events are boss cards with A/B/C action cards (one GRATIS). On the year map future bosses lie face down: you know when, not what. Krisekort and kortvarsel are wild cards that can be shuffled in.
  • Oppgjør: results resolve as a tally, balance before → after, a "SPILT" stamp, and ÅPNET/LUKKET cards.
  • Echo badges are chain links drawn back to the causing card ("Ekko fra mnd 1: gaming-PC fra pengegaven"); Hvorfor? is one tap away.
  • Belongings are relics: gold cards with ongoing effects ("+7 kr/mnd rente", "−249 kr/mnd"). Locked relics wait on the board, and open offers preview their running cost ("Moped etterpå: −1 245 kr/mnd"), making months-ahead thinking concrete.

Visual language

Dark felt table, cream card stock, chunky ink frames, soft shadows. Rarity colour always paired with shape and label: Hendelse red hexagon, Invitasjon mint diamond, Tilbud cobalt triangle, Eiendel gold star, Krise pink octagon, Låst hatching + padlock. Archivo Black for numbers/titles, Archivo Narrow for card text. Original flat vector art. Motion: cards deal in, snap into slots, tally lines count up.

Why it works for 15–20

Card games are a grammar they already read; cost, stats and lasting effects make money literacy feel like a run, not a budget.

Risks

The metaphor can make money abstract (kroner stay prominent); card density at 320 px; "lower stress is better" must be taught early.

Prototype first

Month plan tap-card/tap-slot with running total, then the event tally with echo chain.

Konsept 8 av 8

Linjekart

Fem år. Seksti stopp. Du velger sporet.

The idea. Five years of life drawn as a transit line diagram. The 60 months are stations on Hovedlinja. Highlight events are interchange stations. Age unlocks are new lines that branch off: Mopedlinja from 16, Kortlinja from 18. The pengegave choice can put you on Sparelinja, which runs alongside the main line. The hub is "Neste stasjon", a departure board with your numbers. The year view is the line map itself, and the month plan is a ticket with seats.

Game dynamics. Each month you arrive at a station. A quiet month shows a quiet board ("STILLE MÅNED · ingen hendelse"), and you can leave in one tap ("Fortsett til april"). An active month is an interchange: the event screen draws a junction that splits into one coloured track per option. Each track ends at an option that states its kroner and wellbeing effect, so choosing is literally switching track. On the result screen the tracks you didn't take turn grey and yours carries on. An echo badge is a dashed loop line back to an earlier station ("Ekko fra februar: du lot jakka ligge…"). "Hvorfor?" sits right under the deltas. "Åpnet" and "Lukket" use transit grammar: a line that keeps going vs. a terminus bar. The month plan's seats make time visible: extra shifts hatch out seat 4 ("Tatt av ekstravakter"), and an activity you can't afford shows "Mangler 288 kr" instead of a place button. The room is a flat pictogram drawing with an empty dashed "LEDIG PLASS" where the moped will go, a goal you can see. Unlocks you haven't reached yet show as dashed future lines on the map, which acts as a teaser all the time.

Visual language. Swiss/international style on white. Strict 20px margins, bold flat line colours (cobalt, green, amber, magenta), black interchange rings, and one amber-on-black departure board as the "now" surface. Schibsted Grotesk (a Norwegian grotesk) does the talking. JetBrains Mono is used only for figures, months and board data. Nothing relies on colour alone: hatching marks crisis and missing money, dashes mark echoes and the future, and every delta has a sign and a word. Motion would come from the line: on Continue the station marker slides one tick along the line, and new branches draw themselves in.

Why it works for 15–20. It looks design-literate and grown-up, not childish or like a bank. Teens already read line maps every day on the bus, which is where they will play. "Five years, sixty stops" makes the whole game understandable in one image.

Risks. It can feel cool and austere, and it lacks warmth and humour. The room and the friends' messages have to carry the personality. Dense screens like the money view push the limits of the 390 px grid. The metaphor is weaker for crisis months, which are drawn as hatched red rings.

Prototype first. The junction → result transition: tap an option, the track lights up, the station marker moves, and the echo loop draws in. Test whether teens read "switching track" as consequence.
